newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wholesale, retail data show demand subdued.
newsitem.headline: German wholesale, retail data show demand subdued.

text.p: German retail sales data for November and the wholesale price index for December released on Thursday continued to give a subdued picture for inflation and consumer demand in Germany.
The Federal Statistics Office in Wiesbaden said that retail sales were down by a real two percent on a year-on-year basis in November, despite the introduction of longer shop hours.
Seasonally adjusted retail sales were up by two percent against October, but not enough to turn around a weak trend for 1996, with sales down by one percent in the first 11 months.
Germany's BGA department store lobby group has already warned that its members had a disastrous Christmas, with sales over the peak shopping period down by 3.4 percent year-on-year.
Meanwhile, wholesale price data for December showed a rise of 0.3 percent month-on-month, while prices were up by 0.5 percent compared to the same month a year earlier.
Averaging out the months of 1996, wholesale prices were down 0.6 percent on the previous year.

Separately, the Bundesbank said in its January monthly report that it expected inflation to remain below two percent for the next two years. High unemployment would minimise domestic risks to that forecast, the report added.
